Raw wastewater is pumped from the collection system to the headworks where it is screened and degritted.
The aeration supply of the basins is designed to provide aerobic and anoxic zones to achieve nitrification and denitrification.
A 120-foot diameter secondary clarifier was constructed in addition to the existing clarifier.
Effluent from the secondary clarifier is pumped through cloth media filters prior to UV disinfection.
Cloth media filters and a ultraviolet light (UV) disinfection system were installed to protect shallow groundwater from coliform organism contamination.

As part of the WWTP upgrades, an additional screw press was added and both screw presses with auxiliary equipment (flocculation tanks, polymer system and sludge feed pump) were installed under a permanent canopy structure.

The sludge drying beds are uncovered and may be used in the summer for additional drying or for backup dewatering.
The sludge storage tank is used for emergency storage of wasted sludge in-case of dewatering system failure.
Dewatered sludge is disposed by hauling to a local landfill.
Disinfected effluent is discharged to eleven rapid infiltration ponds (Ponds 1, 2, 4, 5, and 8 through 14).
